findings.where: Screen 4 (Which box?), the main picture before Check
findings.what: The picture marks -Y2 on but draws the relief path bold and prints 'The pump's oil goes over the relief valve.', which contradicts the question's premise and makes the wrong choice 'Straight to T' look right, so draw the lines idle and hide the status line until Check.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Held is not sealed), and screens 1 and 3
findings.what: 'Spool' first appears on screen 9 as an amber term that no screen explains, and a steps lesson shows only the frame, so the explain's definition never reaches him; add one sentence on screen 3 such as 'Inside the valve a grooved rod, the spool, slides in a fixed body. The row of boxes stands for it.'

findings.where: Screen 7 (The middle box), text and sayMain
findings.what: It says a closed centre sends the pump's oil over the relief valve without 'with a fixed pump', which the explain and the common-mistakes list both keep.

It says what each centre does but not why a designer would pick one: P to T spares the pump working against the relief valve, while closed keeps pressure ready for other valves; one short sentence would complete the why.

findings.where: Screen 10 (Will it hold?), hint on 'Yes, as long as the pump keeps running'
findings.what: 'The pump's oil cannot reach A or B' is absolute and sits against the lesson's own point that a real spool leaks between ports, and it switches to 'ram' where every other screen says rod or cylinder; try 'The box blocks P from A and B, so the pump is not what holds the load up.'
'A check valve that a pilot line opens for lowering' uses 'pilot line', which no screen of this lesson has explained.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Held is not sealed) and screen 10 after Check
findings.what: The creep runs the rod fully in within about ten seconds and no on-screen word says it is sped up, while the text says 'creeps slowly' as a certainty; add 'Here the creep is sped up' and say 'can creep'.

The main picture fades in on the Closed centre with oil over the relief valve for about half a second before it switches to P to T, the answer he just gave, and the picture's growth from 152 to 394 units pushes the feedback down at 360 px; starting it on P to T would avoid the wrong flash.
'The drawing shows it there.' is vague; say 'So the sheet draws the valve with its middle box against the ports.'

findings.where: Caption under the frame, all 13 screens
findings.what: 'Leaks On shows what the ideal symbol leaves out.' shows on ten screens that have no Leaks switch.

Why? can be tapped before Check and its text states the figure ('Two boxes make two positions', 'five ports'); it shows only on request, but showing Why? after the first answer would keep the typed figure hidden.

The ports-and-positions slip in the label's order (a 4/2 read as 2/4) is never asked; screens 2 and 13 ask each count on its own, and a pick puzzle 'Which label fits this valve: 4/2 or 2/4?' would test the order directly.

The intermediate-switch bridge from his own wiring appears on no screen of the steps lesson, though one line in screen 2's Why would land it; and its 'breaks' line about mains reversing is beside the point, since the switch works the same on DC, so name the real difference: a switch has no blocked ports and no centre.
The footnote sits on a plain statement ('so the rod comes out') rather than a rule or value he would look up, and it cites a pneumatics text for a hydraulic sentence.

The 360 'moved' and 'end' shots caught screens 2 and 13 unanswered, so the only views of the main valve shifted with flow lit were the thumbnail contact sheets; the moved state could only be checked from the code and the sheets.
